questions.question: Name principal package components and their responsibilities.
questions.answer: vitest is the core testing framework package: its node Vitest.start coordinates reporter and coverage initialization and test execution, and its internal runtime runner startTests collects and runs files. The runner source is inside packages/vitest/src/runtime/runner at this pin; do not invent a separate packages/runner package. @vitest/browser exposes browser-provider utilities; browser-playwright runs tests with Playwright and browser-preview previews tests in a real browser. @vitest/ui displays test results in the browser and exposes a reporter entrypoint. @vitest/expect supplies Jest expect matchers as a Chai plugin; @vitest/snapshot manages snapshots; @vitest/spy provides lightweight Jest-compatible spies. Equivalent source-grounded component terminology is accepted; this is a principal-component overview, not a requirement to enumerate every package or proof that any test was executed.

# @vitest/browser

[![NPM version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@vitest/browser?color=a1b858&label=)](https://npmx.dev/package/@vitest/browser)

This package exposes utilities to make your own browser provider. If you just need to run tests in the browser, consider installing one of these packages instead:

- [@vitest/browser-playwright](https://npmx.dev/package/@vitest/browser-playwright) - run tests using [playwright](https://playwright.dev/)
- [@vitest/browser-webdriverio](https://npmx.dev/package/@vitest/browser-webdriverio) - run tests using [webdriverio](https://webdriver.io/)
- [@vitest/browser-preview](https://npmx.dev/package/@vitest/browser-preview) to see how your tests look like in a real browser.

questions.question: Which languages, build systems and package boundaries organize it?
questions.answer: This is a pnpm workspace monorepo with TypeScript sources and ESM packages. The root scripts recursively build packages and run TypeScript typechecking; vitest builds with Rollup. questions.question: For R, parseCLI("vitest run"), give the source-supported path and outcome, including unresolved boundaries.
questions.answer: parseCLI converts the string using splitArgv, requires vitest as the first token, replaces it with /index.js and prepends node. It calls createCLI(config).parse(arrayArgs,{run:false}); createCLI builds the cac CLI and registers run. parseCLI sets options.run=true when watch is not set and returns filter and options; the fixture expects an empty filter and run:true. CAC parsing is an external-library boundary, and run:false means this path does not establish test execution. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

questions.question: Where does Z, a string argv supplied to parseCLI, enter and get transformed?
questions.answer: parseCLI accepts string or string[]; a string is sent to splitArgv. splitArgv temporarily protects spaces in quoted substrings, splits on spaces, restores protected spaces and invokes removeQuotes. parseCLI validates the leading vitest token, rewrites the program prefix and hands tokens to CAC with execution disabled.
